work.text: Le Pilote de Tonga, a prose poem in a frame, etched in 1856, is the first of what grew, in the sixties, into a long series of etchings founded on his sketches and reminiscences of his early voyage to the South Seas.
Throughout his voyage on the Rhin he made drawings, many of which he turned into etchings some twenty years later.

moment.text: The French base in New Zealand was Akaroa, or Port Louis-Philippe as the French still called it, then a small whaling-station, with a mostly French population.

matters.text: Distorted in form and pinched and puny from its birth, I could not but pity it … could not deny it a place in my souvenirs de voyage, and so I drew it carefully.

matters.text: Long afterwards, in conversations with Burty, Meryon used to say how his thoughts dwelt on the rocky coast of New [Caledonia] … where he had breathed an air overladen with balm, where, if he could, he should like one day to return to finish life free and happy.
